target.question: Which deployed change accounts for the new checkout latency regression, and what bounded causal evidence distinguishes it from load variation?

native_baseline.target_task: Which deployed change accounts for the new checkout latency regression, and what bounded causal evidence distinguishes it from load variation?
native_baseline.reference_practitioner: Production reliability engineer specializing in web-service incident diagnosis.
ordinary_methods: Compare deployment and latency timelines, stratifying traffic and configuration.
Replay representative workloads, bisect revisions and test competing causes in staging.
Use rollback and controlled reintroduction when safe; inspect traces and resource metrics.
ordinary_evidence: Version and configuration history; request traces; latency distributions; resource counters.
uncertainty: Scoped authored hypothesis, not verified practitioner consensus.
Teams differ in experimental maturity; this scope includes ordinary staging experiments but no formal inverse-problem specialty.

facts: Authored synthetic environment; no real persons or organizations.
Configurations old and new differ only in the deployed cache-policy flag. Live traffic volume also changed, so the live association alone is confounded.
An isolated resettable replay can cross either configuration with low or high load on any listed route. A route trial returns endpoint latency in ms.

Independent calibration in this replay established an additive service-delay model at fixed load, endpoint measurement error bounded by 1 ms, and stable route membership. Calibration does not reveal current component delays.
Candidate explanations are a deployment effect on the B-containing dependency, a deployment effect confined to A, and load-only variation. Alternatives may be incomplete.

deployment_log: old then new cache-policy flag; no other configuration change

initial_observations: The aggregate live route-r1 latency rose by 30 ms; attribution and component contributions are unresolved.
known_uncertainties: No component-level timings are available. Replay effects need not generalize to every live workload.
constraints: No internal service probes or live deployment changes.
All analyses use the same supplied route catalog.

other_constraints: Both branches start from an independent reset of this same world.
A procedure may contain elementary trials, but all consume the common ledger.
Unused resources are allowed; proposed later inquiries are not performed within this budget.
